titular: Nvidia plunges after hours as board reportedly prepares to oust Jensen Huang
resum: According to The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia's board is preparing to remove its chief executive and founder, Jensen Huang, after two extramarital affairs came to light. The shares fell 8% in after-hours trading to about $160, and are down 23% since 3 November.
per_que_importa: Nvidia makes the chips that power artificial intelligence and is one of the heaviest weights in stock indices and in many funds and pension plans. A sudden change at the top can hit the whole tech sector and, by knock-on effect, many people's savings.
xifra_text: Nvidia's after-hours drop on Wednesday, following the WSJ report

titular: Wall Street bounces back strongly thanks to CoreWeave
resum: The Nasdaq rose 1.60% on Wednesday to 25,466 points and the S&P 500 gained 1.29% to 7,618, a day after the inflation-driven sell-off. Data-centre company CoreWeave soared 24.71% after better-than-expected results, and Apple hit a new record.
per_que_importa: When a key AI company shows it is earning more than expected, investors regain confidence in the whole sector. But such sharp swings from one day to the next are a reminder that, in the short term, the stock market moves a lot on mood.
xifra_text: Nasdaq's gain on Wednesday, the day after a losing session

titular: European stocks close at a record, led by Siemens Energy
resum: The Stoxx 600 index rose 0.72% on Wednesday to 663.05 points, its best close ever. Siemens Energy jumped 10.8% after reporting a record year, targeting a 20–22% profit margin by 2030 and announcing up to €9bn more to buy back its own shares.
per_que_importa: Siemens Energy makes turbines and power-grid equipment, which are in high demand because of data centres. A European manufacturer earning more means investment and jobs in Europe, not just at US tech giants.
xifra_text: Stoxx 600 points, its highest close ever

titular: Spain's Ibex closes above 20,000 points despite the general strike
resum: The Ibex 35 rose 0.46% on Wednesday to 20,027.90 points, closing above that level in the middle of a strike day. ACS (+3.11%), Repsol (+3.03%) and Telefónica (+2.13%) led the gains, while Aena fell 1.31%.
per_que_importa: The Ibex brings together Spain's biggest companies, such as banks, builders and energy firms, and its value feeds into many pension plans and funds. The fact that the market shrugged off the strike shows investors are mainly watching company profits and the global backdrop.

titular: More Fed officials call for rate hikes after the inflation data
resum: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called October's inflation figure "borderline disturbing", and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said she favours raising rates at least two more times. Futures markets now fully price in a hike in December.
per_que_importa: When the Fed raises rates, borrowing gets more expensive in the US and that drags up the cost of money worldwide. If hikes come quickly, companies may put investment and hiring on hold.
xifra_text: current Fed rate range, which markets expect to rise in December

titular: Spain's general strike ends with clashing turnout figures
resum: Employers' group CEOE says turnout in the strike over housing and wages was below 5% and calls it a failure, while the UGT union gives a "very positive" assessment. The Interior Ministry counted 53 arrests and 1,044 incidents across Spain by 8 pm, with road blockades and rioting in Barcelona.
per_que_importa: The strike highlights two underlying problems: housing costs and wages that don't keep up with inflation. How they are tackled (more homes, higher pay or more subsidies) will affect many household budgets and business costs.
xifra_text: strike turnout according to employers; unions claim success

titular: Asia shrugs off the Nvidia shock
resum: South Korea's Kospi rose 2.60% on Wednesday to 5,375.36 points and opened slightly higher on Thursday, as did Tokyo (Nikkei +0.23%). Samsung is up 1.7%, while Kioxia and SoftBank, more closely tied to Nvidia and AI, are down about 2%.
per_que_importa: Korea and Japan make much of the memory and components that go into AI chips. Whatever happens at Nvidia quickly reaches these companies and their supply chains, and from there electronics prices.
xifra_text: Korea's Kospi gain on Wednesday, before the Nvidia news

titular: Oil edges up as new attacks on ships hit Hormuz
resum: Brent rose 0.2% on Wednesday to $91.68 a barrel and US WTI stood at $85.98. Fresh attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz offset hopes of a truce with Iran, after Brent dipped below $90 during Tuesday's session for the first time since August.
per_que_importa: A large share of the world's oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz. Every scare there shows up in petrol prices, diesel for freight and, in the end, inflation.
xifra_text: price of a barrel of Brent on Wednesday

titular: Today: Telefónica results and UK GDP
resum: Telefónica reports its nine-month results at 7.30 am, as do ACS, Acciona, CAF and Talgo. At 8 am (Spanish time) comes the first estimate of UK third-quarter GDP, and Spain's parliament votes on housing decrees just before the election campaign begins.
per_que_importa: Results from big Spanish companies show how sales, profits and investment and hiring plans are going in the country. And the housing decrees could directly affect rents and home purchases.
xifra_text: time Telefónica publishes its results (Spanish time)
